key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving electronic uniformity, showing that surface smoothness is not a reliable proxy for optoelectronic quality.
engineering_relevance: Mixed-dimensional capping offers a route to more durable perovskite photovoltaics by suppressing non-radiative recombination and aging-induced electronic disorder.
method: Combine statistical AFM with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare morphology, emission, and quasi-Fermi level splitting before and after accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films showed enhanced photoluminescence, more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, and better preservation of optoelectronic homogeneity during accelerated aging than pristine films.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative device-efficiency or operational-lifetime results, so photovoltaic performance gains remain unverified here.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
